## QueryObject::Filter is a bare *FilterCondition for most /query types, so backends can never receive AND/OR/NOT trees
Crates: jmap-mail-types, jmap-contacts-types, jmap-calendars-types, jmap-tasks-types, jmap-filenode-types (and the matching *-server crates whose handlers/backends use O::Filter)
Evidence: `type Filter =` uses the bare condition at crate-jmap-mail-types/src/backend.rs:220 (Mailbox), crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/backend.rs:227/243/263 (Calendar, CalendarEvent, CalendarEventNotification), crate-jmap-contacts-types/src/backend.rs:139 (ContactCard), crate-jmap-tasks-types/src/backend.rs:256/272 (Task, TaskNotification), crate-jmap-filenode-types/src/backend.rs:68 (FileNode). Within the canonical crate, Email uses the full tree (`EmailFilter`, mail-types backend.rs:243), and so do EmailSubmission (:270) and all of chat/scene/vtc/graph. The full-tree aliases already exist but are unused here: MailboxFilter (mail-types query.rs:23), CalendarFilter (calendar.rs:231), CalendarEventFilter (event.rs:448), ContactCardFilter (card.rs:538), FileNodeFilter (filter.rs:155). The spec types every /query filter as `FilterOperator|FilterCondition|null` (RFC 8620 line 2368; the /queryChanges filter at line 2649). draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-33 line 2159 only requires a bare FilterCondition when `expandRecurrences` is true, which implies operators are normally allowed. The in-workspace clients now send `Filter<C>` trees for all these methods (CHANGELOG.md ~2943-2955). Probe result: `ContactCard/query` with `{"operator":"OR",...}` returns `unsupportedFilter`, and `CalendarEvent/query` with AND returns `unsupportedFilter: unknown field conditions`.
Why breaking later: `QueryObject::Filter` is a public associated type, and every backend's `query_objects::<O>` / `query_changes::<O>` receives `Option<&O::Filter>`. Moving it from `XxxFilterCondition` to `Filter<XxxFilterCondition>` changes the type that every downstream backend matches on. The default `FileNodeBackend::query_subtree` (crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/backend.rs:623) builds a bare `FileNodeFilterCondition` and passes it as `O::Filter`, so that changes too. After 0.4 the fix cannot be done without a semver break, and until it is, the workspace's own clients get unsupportedFilter for standard operator queries.
Fix: Set `type Filter = XxxFilter` (the existing `Filter<XxxFilterCondition>` alias) for Mailbox, Calendar, CalendarEvent, CalendarEventNotification, ContactCard, Task, TaskNotification and FileNode, to match the canonical Email. Handlers decode with `filter_arg::<XxxFilter>`. Backends that cannot evaluate operators return `BackendQueryError::Method(unsupportedFilter)` themselves. CalendarEvent/query keeps its expandRecurrences rule as a handler check (`Filter::Condition` only). Update query_subtree to wrap its condition in `Filter::Condition`.
